name: Toast
purpose: A brief message confirming that an action finished, such as Changes saved, which disappears on its own.
description: Transient confirmation after an action. The message is announced through a live status region without moving focus.

guidance.summary: A brief message confirming that an action finished, such as Changes saved, which disappears on its own.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person just took succeeded, when the result is not visible otherwise.
The message is a few words and needs no response.

avoidWhen.text: An error the person has to fix.
A decision the person must make, or an action to confirm.
Messages that must stay until read, or several that arrive together.
The result is already visible where the person is looking. Show nothing extra.

states.label: Hidden
states.description: No message; the live region waits, empty.

states.label: Visible
states.description: The message appears at the bottom of the screen, is announced without moving focus, and fades after about four seconds.
states.how: An action that succeeded calls the toast with its message.

states.label: Replaced
states.description: A new message replaces the current one and restarts the timer; toasts never pile up.
states.how: A second action within four seconds.

dos.text: Confirm the result in a few words, in the past tense: Changes saved, Invite sent.
dos.why: People glance at it; it has to be read in under two seconds.

dos.text: Show it only once the action has actually succeeded.
dos.why: A toast that confirms something that then fails breaks trust.

dos.text: Keep what the toast says available elsewhere on the page.
dos.why: It disappears on its own, so people who missed it must still be able to find the result.

donts.text: Don’t use a toast for errors or warnings.
donts.why: It vanishes before people can act, and an error belongs next to what caused it.

donts.text: Don’t put links or buttons in a toast.
donts.why: It disappears on a timer, often before keyboard and screen reader users can reach it.

donts.text: Don’t show a toast for every small change.
donts.why: Frequent toasts become noise and teach people to ignore them.

content: Past tense, sentence case, no end punctuation: Project created.
Name the object when it helps: Invite sent to ana@example.com.

notes: The message is written into a role="status" live region, so screen readers announce it politely without moving focus.
It stays about four seconds. Anything people need later must be on the page too, because they cannot pause or recall a toast.
